ops.title: The payload fetch gives each range a FIFO the script opens first
ops.body:
Supersedes the mechanism in note fb51924 (its reasons for memory buffers, no signals, and the piped config still hold). Each range is curl | dd bs=<range> iflag=fullblock >&<writer fd>, where the script made one FIFO, opened it read-write, then read-only and write-only, closed the read-write fd, and unlinked the path before starting the range. The consumer reads the read fd to EOF and then waits for the job.

Why: an earlier form ended each job with cat > FIFO, which blocks in open() until the consumer arrives. A sol review found that a writer killed while blocked there leaves the consumer waiting forever. With both ends open up front nothing blocks in open, and a dead range closes its write end, so the consumer sees EOF and wait reports the status.

Later ranges inherit the read ends of earlier pending ranges, so closing a read end does not SIGPIPE its writer. A failed download therefore reads the in-flight ranges to EOF and then waits; it must not just close them.

Measured on one Sprite, 2.13 GB, SHA checked: 11.83 s; a broken-signature URL fails in 0.48 s with HTTP 403 and leaves nothing.
